# Introduction by the Author
Dear Reader,

As an educator and a lifelong admirer of English literature, I have always been passionate about helping students engage with classic works in meaningful ways. With this goal in mind, I am delighted to present "An Objective Approach to Mayor of Casterbridge: MCQs for RPSC Exams."

This book is the result of my years of experience teaching and studying Thomas Hardy's timeless novel, "The Mayor of Casterbridge." I have found that one of the most effective ways to deepen one's understanding of a literary work is through the practice of answering focused, thought-provoking questions. This is particularly true when preparing for exams like the RPSC First Grade Exam, where a strong grasp of the material is essential for success.

In creating this book, I have carefully crafted 47 sets of multiple-choice questions that cover a wide range of topics related to "The Mayor of Casterbridge." Each set is designed to test your knowledge of the novel's plot, characters, themes, and literary devices. By working through these questions, you will not only reinforce your understanding of the book but also identify areas where you may need to focus your study efforts.

My aim with this book is to provide you with a valuable resource that will help you approach your RPSC First Grade exam with confidence. Whether you are a student preparing for the RPSC First Grade Exam or simply a reader looking to engage with Hardy's work on a deeper level, I believe that "An Objective Approach to Mayor of Casterbridge" will be an invaluable companion on your journey.
I wish you all the best in your studies and in your future endeavors. Happy reading and learning!
Sincerely,
Mukesh K Sharma
# Set: 1
Q1: What time period does the story take place in?
A) Early 17th century
B) Early 18th century
C) Early 19th century
D) Early 20th century
Answer: C
Q2: Where were the young man and woman approaching?
A) Lower Wessex
B) Weydon-Priors
C) Upper Sussex
D) Weatherbury
Answer: B
Q3: What was the man carrying on his back?
A) A knapsack
B) A rush basket
C) A leather satchel
D) A canvas bag
Answer: B
Q4: What was visible protruding from the man's basket?
A) A scythe
B) A hay-knife
C) A pitchfork
D) A sickle
Answer: B
Q5: What was peculiar about the couple's progress?
A) They walked very quickly
B) They frequently stopped to rest
C) They preserved perfect silence
D) They took a winding, indirect route
Answer: C
Q6: What was the chief attraction of the young woman's face?
A) Its mobility
B) Its paleness
C) Its perfect symmetry
D) Its delicate features
Answer: A
Q7: What was the little girl wearing on her feet?
A) Leather boots
B) Wooden clogs
C) Blue knitted yarn boots
D) Cloth slippers
Answer: C
Q8: What event was taking place in the village that day?
A) A harvest festival
B) A wedding
C) A fair
D) A funeral
Answer: C
Q9: What refreshment did the couple seek at the fair?
A) Roasted chestnuts
B) Meat pies
C) Furmity
D) Cider
Answer: C
Q10: Who presided over the furmity tent?
A) A young maiden
B) A jolly farmer
C) A haggish creature of about fifty
D) An elderly gentleman
Answer: C
Q11: What did the man secretly have added to his furmity?
A) Sugar
B) Rum
C) Cream
D) Spices
Answer: B
Q12: How did the man's demeanor change after drinking the laced furmity?
A) He became sleepy
B) He turned sullen and withdrawn
C) He grew overbearing and quarrelsome
D) He became overly affectionate
Answer: C
Q13: What was the theme of the conversation that arose?
A) The ruin of good men by bad wives
B) The joys of love and marriage
C) The importance of sobriety
D) The changing times
Answer: A
Q14: How much money did the man claim to have?
A) Less than five shillings
B) No more than ten shillings
C) Not more than fifteen shillings
D) At least twenty shillings
Answer: C
Q15: What shocking suggestion did the man make regarding wives?
A) That they should be cherished and adored
B) That they should manage the household finances
C) That they should be sold at auction
D) That they should work outside the home
Answer: C
Q16: Who praised the man's wife as having "true cultivation"?
A) A well-dressed gentleman
B) A smoking man who seemed a former servant
C) The furmity seller
D) One of the rustic locals
Answer: B
Q17: How much did the man initially offer to sell his wife for?
A) Five shillings
B) One guinea
C) Three guineas
D) Five guineas
Answer: D
Q18: Who unexpectedly agreed to buy the man's wife?
A) A wealthy farmer
B) The smoking gentleman
C) A sailor
D) The furmity seller
Answer: C
Q19: How much did the sailor pay for the wife?
A) Three guineas
B) Four pounds
C) Five guineas
D) Ten pounds
Answer: C
Q20: What did the woman do before leaving with the sailor?
A) Embraced her husband
B) Collected her belongings
C) Threw her wedding ring at her husband
D) Pleaded with her husband to reconsider
Answer: C
Q21: What did the woman take with her when she left?
A) A trunk of clothing
B) The furmity pot
C) Her child Elizabeth-Jane
D) The family dog
Answer: C
Q22: How did the husband react to his wife's departure?
A) With relief and joy
B) With a stolid look of concern
C) With anger and threats
D) With tears and pleas
Answer: B
Q23: What was notable about the horses outside the tent?
A) They were fighting amongst themselves
B) They were beautifully adorned with ribbons
C) They were waiting patiently to be harnessed
D) They were running loose without tethers
Answer: C
Q24: What did the husband vow regarding his wife?
A) That he would win her back
B) That he would seek revenge on the sailor
C) That he would not go after her
D) That he would leave town himself
Answer: C
Q25: Why did the furmity seller decide to let the man sleep in the tent?
A) She pitied his drunken state
B) He had paid her handsomely
C) The fair was continuing for several more days
D) She hoped he would buy more furmity in the morning
Answer: C
Q26: What color were the clouds in the west after sunset?
A) Rosy
B) Golden
C) Gray
D) Purple
Answer: A
Q27: How long had the woman been married to the man?
A) Six months
B) A year
C) A couple of years
D) Five years
Answer: C
Q28: What was the hay-trusser's trade?
A) Threshing wheat
B) Tending livestock
C) Cutting and bundling hay
D) Planting crops
Answer: C
Q29: What instrument was used to stir the furmity mixture?
A) A wooden spoon
B) A metal ladle
C) A large spoon
D) A long paddle
Answer: C
Q30: At what age did the man say he had married?
A) Sixteen
B) Eighteen
C) Twenty
D) Twenty-two
Answer: B

Q1: What was the man's name?
A) Michael Henchard
B) John Melvin
C) Thomas Briggs
D) William Dorset
Answer: A
Q2: What did the man see shining on the ground?
A) A gold coin
B) His wife's ring
C) A silver necklace
D) A metal button
Answer: B
Q3: What was the man carrying on his shoulders?
A) A sack of tools
B) A backpack
C) A basket of tools
D) A heavy bag
Answer: C
Q4: What kind of animal was the man's dog compared to?
A) A wolf
B) A fox
C) A cat
D) A bear
Answer: B
Q5: What was the man's occupation?
A) Farmer
B) Carpenter
C) Blacksmith
D) Hay-trusser
Answer: D
Q6: What was the man's wife's name?
A) Susan
B) Elizabeth
C) Mary
D) Jane
Answer: A
Q7: What did the man say he would do with his wife?
A) Divorce her
B) Sell her
C) Abandon her
D) Imprison her
Answer: B
Q8: Where did the man go after leaving the fair?
A) The village
B) The church
C) The pub
D) The market
Answer: B
Q9: What was the man's oath about?
A) Avoiding alcohol for 21 years
B) Being kind to his family
C) Finding his wife and child
D) Becoming a better person
Answer: A
Q10: What was the man's plan after making the oath?
A) Settle in Casterbridge
B) Return to the fair
C) Search for his wife and child
D) Find a new job
Answer: C
Q11: What did the man notice about the cottage's chimney?
A) It was emitting smoke
B) It was partially collapsed
C) It was unusually tall
D) It had no smoke coming from it
Answer: A
Q12: How did the man pay for his breakfast?
A) With coins
B) With the sailor's money
C) With a trifling payment
D) By doing chores for the housewife
Answer: C
Q13: How long did the man search for his wife and child?
A) A few days
B) A couple of weeks
C) Months
D) Years
Answer: C
Q14: What information did the man get at the seaport?
A) His wife and child had moved away
B) His wife and child had been found
C) His wife and child had emigrated
D) His wife and child were staying with the sailor
Answer: C
Q15: Where did the man decide to settle after his search?
A) Casterbridge
B) The village near the fair
C) The seaport town
D) His hometown
Answer: A
Q16: Where did the man wake up in the morning?
A) In his own bed
B) In a tent
C) On the ground
D) In a wagon
Answer: B
Q17: What was the man's initial reaction to realizing his wife was gone?
A) Happiness
B) Anger
C) Confusion
D) Sadness
Answer: C
Q18: What did the man say his wife's actions showed about her character?
A) She was reckless and resentful
B) She was meek and submissive
C) She was intelligent and cunning
D) She was foolish and simple
Answer: D
Q19: What did the man do after making his oath in the church?
A) He went to search for his wife
B) He went to find a job
C) He went to the village pub
D) He went to board a ship
Answer: A
Q20: What was unusual about the dogs the man saw at the fair?
A) They were aggressive and loud
B) They were well-trained and obedient
C) They were of mysterious breeds
D) They were small and timid
Answer: C
Q21: What time of day was it when the man left the fair?
A) Early morning
B) Midday
C) Evening
D) Late at night
Answer: A
Q22: What was the man's initial plan after realizing his wife was gone?
A) To go to the police
B) To get a job and save money
C) To get out of the situation as soon as possible
D) To return to the fair and search for her
Answer: C
Q23: What was the man's reaction to his wife's actions?
A) He was surprised and annoyed
B) He was understanding and forgiving
C) He was ashamed and embarrassed
D) He was relieved and indifferent
Answer: A
Q24: What was the man's reason for not following the investigation loudly?
A) He was afraid of the consequences
B) He was shy about revealing his conduct
C) He didn't have the resources to do so
D) He didn't care about finding his wife
Answer: B
Q25: What did the man notice about the village when he arrived?
A) It was bustling and active
B) It was quiet and still
C) It was deserted and abandoned
D) It was covered in a heavy fog
Answer: B
Q26: What was the significance of the man making his oath in the church?
A) It was a symbolic act of repentance
B) It was a necessary legal requirement
C) It was a personal tradition for him
D) It was a way to seek divine intervention
Answer: A
Q27: What was the man's final attitude towards his wife's actions?
A) He blamed her entirely
B) He took responsibility for them
C) He was indifferent to them
D) He didn't understand them
Answer: B
Q28: What was the man's primary motivation for searching for his wife and child?
A) To get his money back
B) To bring them home
C) To punish his wife
D) To clear his own name
Answer: B
Q29: What was the man's initial reaction to the events of the previous evening?
A) He was shocked and dismayed
B) He was amused and indifferent
C) He was curious and interested
D) He was relieved and content
Answer: A
Q30: What was the man's plan for settling in Casterbridge?
A) To start a new business
B) To find work as a laborer
C) To live a quiet, solitary life
D) To search for his family again
Answer: C
